questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-autoplan-chain on main, about to /autoplan the User Dashboard plan.
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules. This repo has no CLAUDE.md yet. Routing rules tell the agent which skill to reach for (bugs → /investigate, ship → /ship) so you don't have to name skills by hand. Stakes: without it, skills only run when you invoke them explicitly.
Stakes if we pick wrong: mild — either a small extra file in the repo, or slightly more manual skill invocation.
Recommendation: A because routing rules are a one-time, low-cost file that makes every future session smoother.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: a committed CLAUDE.md section vs. manual skill invocation. Note: we are in plan mode, so the file write and commit happen after plan approval, not now.

options.label: Add routing rules to CLAUDE.md (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Future requests auto-route to the right skill without you naming it. ✅ One-time setup, committed once, shared with teammates. ❌ Adds a CLAUDE.md file to a repo that has none today (written after plan approval).

options.label: No thanks, I'll invoke skills manually
options.description: ✅ Repo stays minimal, no new files added. ✅ You keep full control over when skills run. ❌ Skills never fire proactively; you type each one yourself.

questions.question:
D2 — Run /office-hours first for a design doc?
Project/branch/task: same repo, no design doc found for this branch.
ELI10: No design doc found for this branch. /office-hours produces a structured problem statement, premise challenge, and explored alternatives — it gives this review much sharper input to work with. Takes about 10 minutes. The design doc is per-feature, not per-product — it captures the thinking behind this specific change. Stakes: the CEO review phase leans on a design doc to judge premises; without one it works from the plan text alone.
Stakes if we pick wrong: either 10 extra minutes up front, or a CEO review with slightly less context on why this dashboard exists.
Recommendation: B because the plan already carries a detailed 'Existing product and application contracts' section with the problem (75s median to find next task), success metric (45s), and guardrails, which is most of what office-hours would produce.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=8/10
Net: 10 minutes of upfront problem framing vs. proceeding on an already well-grounded plan.

options.label: Run /office-hours now
options.description: ✅ Produces a formal problem statement and alternatives the CEO review can challenge directly. ✅ Leaves a committed design doc for teammates. ❌ Adds ~10 minutes (human: ~30 min / CC: ~10 min) before the review starts, and this plan already states its problem and metric.

options.label: Skip — proceed with standard review (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Review starts immediately using the plan's existing problem statement and success metrics. ✅ The plan's contracts section already covers most of what office-hours would surface. ❌ No separate design doc artifact; premise challenge works from plan text only.
